channel.title: Ivor Benko — Blog
channel.description: Skipper on sailboats and catamarans in Croatia

item.title: From ski instructor to skipper: how I ended up at sea
item.description: Ivor Benko is a Croatian skipper from Zagreb. He grew up skiing, became a licensed ISIA ski instructor, discovered sailing while studying at the Faculty of Kinesiology in Zagreb, and has worked as a skipper on sailboats and catamarans in the Adriatic since 2020.

item.title: What to pack for a week of sailing in Croatia
item.description: Pack light in a soft bag, bring non-marking shoes, strong sun protection, a warm layer and a windproof jacket for the evenings, a power bank and your documents. Leave the hard suitcase and most of your wardrobe at home.

item.title: Sailing the Kornati: a skipper's guide to the national park
item.description: The Kornati National Park is a maze of 89 islands, islets and reefs in central Dalmatia, and one of the best sailing areas in Croatia. Start from Murter or another nearby base, buy the park ticket before you enter, fill up water and fuel beforehand, and plan anchorages around the wind.

item.title: Catamaran or sailboat for a charter in Croatia?
item.description: Choose a catamaran if you want space, stability at anchor and comfort for a family or a larger group. Choose a monohull sailboat if you want the real feel of sailing, easier berths in busy marinas and a lower price. Both work well in the Adriatic.

item.title: Bura, jugo and maestral: the Adriatic winds explained by a skipper
item.description: Three winds shape sailing in Croatia. Maestral is the friendly northwesterly afternoon breeze of summer. Bura is a cold, gusty northeasterly that can arrive fast and strong. Jugo is a warm southeasterly that builds over a day or two and brings big waves. Skippers plan every route around which one is coming.

item.title: Do you need a skipper for a sailing holiday in Croatia?
item.description: You need a skipper in Croatia if nobody in your group holds a boat licence recognised in Croatia plus a VHF radio certificate. Even with licences, many groups hire one to handle marinas, anchoring and weather, so that everyone else can actually be on holiday.
